final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record. The narrowed position is more accurate than an unconditional certification theory, but it still does not satisfy the missing compliance predicate. On the available evidence, aggregate readiness, monitoring, rollback, and model-card guidance support launch governance generally, and they support the view that disclosure would be the correct path. They do not establish that the required disclosure is actually in place before launch, nor that approved risk acceptance exists, nor that the affected use case is excluded from rollout. That distinction matters: a clearly caveated argument can support a recommendation about what would be needed for compliance, but it is not itself evidence that compliance has been achieved. Because the unresolved predicate remains unproven on the current record, the appropriate final assessment remains suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required pre-launch model-card disclosure has been completed or approved.
The affected e-commerce seller enforcement segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
There is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposed segment; the available draft is unsigned and does not address the exposure.
Policy text states disclosure duties remain when the affected segment is exposed and rollout controls alone do not cure that predicate.
